scope: Remaining #73 acceptance after the archived first pilot: the served HTTPS matrix, the bounded network client, Drift in CI and the measured generation decision. Tests, a CI-only tool, a flake check, documentation and evidence; no endpoint or server behavior change.

acceptance.old_new_matrix_against_real_service_shel: crates/kiln-web-service/tests/http_contract/served_client.rs served_https_matrix_and_complete_or_incomplete_pagination: the real `kiln-web-service serve` process over loopback TLS; five GET bodies validated; real 401, 403 worker_scope, 403 execution_binding_scope, 404 run_missing and 400 page_bound keep distinct classes; pagination reaches its end or is reported incomplete. Tested window: current server and client (lockstep).
acceptance.bounded_bytes_deadlines_no_retries: served_client.rs loopback_tls_replays_captured_body_with_faults_without_retries: success and error bodies capped at CLIENT_BODY_LIMIT independently of Content-Length; named connect, total and body-idle deadlines; mutated bodies are schema_mismatch; mislabeled length, oversized chunked, slow and stalled bodies are transport; the stub counts exactly one request per case.
acceptance.drift_in_ci_with_policy: checks.x86_64-linux.http-contract-drift in flake.nix runs tools/http-contract-drift (Drift dad4f398c10ca53298d2fec0586d834c8e85daf1) on contracts/http-api/baseline/openapi.json versus the committed document and on four fixture pairs, asserting exact exit status, class record and decision; evidence/drift-check.json.
acceptance.unknown_outcomes_preserved: unchanged from the first pilot; docs/http-api-contract.md 'Unknown outcomes and lost observation'
acceptance.build_time_code_volume_and_maintenance: scripts/http-contract-generation-measure.py and evidence/generation-measurement.json: Progenitor b317a865 rejects the unchanged contract (missing operation IDs); with five scratch-only operationId additions it generates 470 lines and 16,940 bytes, adds 74 packages relative to the root lock and built in 57.41 s cold and 0.17 s warm at two jobs, against a 145-line handwritten validator and classifier. Documented no-go in docs/http-api-contract.md.
acceptance.licenses_before_adoption: LICENSES.md records the Drift tool and its transitive licenses; the Progenitor cohort's licenses are inventoried in evidence/generation-measurement.json; nothing generated is adopted.

review_fixes: Real-server requests use a separate, generous deadline profile; the short deadlines apply only to stub faults whose timing the stub controls.

The Drift tool separates policy rejection (exit 1) from usage, input and comparison errors (exit 2), and the flake check asserts exact status, class and decision, so a broken fixture cannot pass as an expected rejection.
Drift fixtures are minimal synthetic document pairs instead of four copies of the contract.
The generation measurement is a committed, portable harness (Cargo from the development shell or --cargo, required --output), and the retained receipt was regenerated from it.

The first workspace-wide test run failed both served-client tests: workspace feature unification enables two rustls crypto providers, so ClientConfig::builder() had no default. The client now installs the ring provider as the service and the other TLS tests do.

checks.result: fail before the provider fix: both served-client tests panicked in rustls crypto provider selection; the run stopped at that binary
pass after the provider fix across 166 test binaries
every new kiln.web.http_contract requirement and scenario referenced; only the pre-existing kiln.github.landing.merge.scenario.landed and kiln.github.source_status.scenario.close remain missing

nix flake check path:$PWD --no-write-lock-file --keep-going -L --option builders '' --option min-free 0 --option max-free 0

non_claims: The bounded client is a test fixture, not a shipped client or hostile-network qualification.
The TLS stub replays a captured real body; it tests client classification, not server behavior for malformed responses.
The tested compatibility window is the current server and client only; retained schemas promise no prior API version.
A changed contract version opens a pending transition that passes incompatible changes against the old baseline until a reviewed baseline replacement closes it; unhandled comparisons always fail.
Drift classifications are bounded by the pinned Drift revision and the committed fixtures, not a proof of semantic compatibility.
Generation timings are single-host observations at two Cargo jobs; no generated client or Progenitor dependency was adopted, and no server was migrated.
